title: NoteManager adaptive substep counters and single-step fallback

constructor.counter_allocation: 0x377E28C..0x377E2A4 allocates a four-element uint array and stores it at +0x78.

bms_analysis.count_write: 0x377D27C..0x377D28C copies the parsed BPM-change count to NoteManager +0x74.

activation.disabled_behavior: When the count is below one, the method uses one update step and does not increment any performance counter.

update_order: force one step when any fallback threshold is reached
divide both deltaTime and ExecuteFrame by the final step count
execute the active-note loop finalStepCount times

fallback.counter_3: counter[3] has no direct fallback comparison
fallback.precedence: The fallback is evaluated after the current bucket increments, so the 101st, 21st, and 6th samples respectively use one step.

lifecycle.initialization: The four counters begin at zero in the constructor-allocated managed array.
lifecycle.reset_search: Static inspection of the NoteManager method range found no replacement or explicit zeroing of the array after construction.
lifecycle.bpm_count: bpmChangeCount is refreshed from parsed BMS data during analyzeBMS rather than inferred from frame timing.

prototype.state: NoteManagerPerformanceState stores the four counters, final update-step count, substep deltaTime and substep ExecuteFrame.
prototype.transition: advance_note_manager_performance implements exact strict bucket comparisons, post-increment fallback thresholds, and disabled behavior.
prototype.runtime: RuntimeIntegration updates the performance state before advancing its deterministic clock and exposes it through snapshot.note_manager.
prototype.tempo_bridge: The backend-neutral TempoMap change count supplies the parsed-BMS count boundary for the executable prototype.
prototype.substep_scope: The prototype preserves the recovered substep values as observable scheduling state while its outer deterministic engine update remains a single call.

confirmed: the adaptive policy uses a persistent four-element uint counter array
bucket comparisons are strict at 0.018, 0.033 and 0.05 seconds
history fallback is based on the updated counters
the first three counters can permanently force subsequent NoteManager updates to one step
the fourth counter is observational and does not directly force fallback
inference: TempoMap.changes length is the prototype equivalent of the parsed BMS bpmChangeCount field.
unresolved: The reason for the asymmetric 100, 20 and 6 sample thresholds is not named in managed metadata.
A backend that reproduces the exact inner active-note loop must execute note state updates once per selected substep rather than only expose the scheduling state.
